highlights_headline: SkiaSharp 4.152.0 brings the Graphite GPU backend, Nano Server font support, and Skia m152.
highlights_body: This release adds next-generation Graphite GPU bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn, a new SkiaSharp.Vulkan.Silk.NET package, and FreeType-backed text on Windows Nano Server. Several memory and allocation fixes land alongside the Skia m152 engine upgrade.

bullets.detail: The bundled Skia engine advances to m152, including upstream chrome/m151 bug-fix syncs carried over from the 4.151.x line.
Binding generation now produces identical output regardless of the build platform, eliminating spurious diffs when regenerating on different OSes.

bullets.lead: Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn
bullets.detail: New bindings expose Skia's next-generation Graphite rendering pipeline. Consumers can create Graphite GPU contexts for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn backends, unlocking a modern, lower-overhead GPU path.

bullets.lead: Backend-neutral async RequestReadPixels on SKImage and SKSurface
bullets.detail: A new async pixel-readback API lets callers read pixel data from GPU-backed images and surfaces without blocking the render thread, working across all supported GPU backends.
A dedicated NuGet package wraps the Silk.NET Vulkan interop layer, making it straightforward to wire up Vulkan contexts without custom P/Invoke boilerplate.
The SKRegion backing the SpanIterator was not rooted and could be collected mid-iteration, causing a native use-after-free crash. The region is now correctly kept alive for the iterator's lifetime.
The pixel source passed to ExtractSubset and With* methods was not rooted and could be garbage-collected before the native call completed.

bullets.lead: Memory leak in SKImage.Create raster failure path fixed
bullets.detail: A CoTaskMem pixel buffer allocated during raster image creation was not freed on native call failure, leading to a silent native memory leak.

bullets.lead: Reduced allocations across text and uniform-lookup paths
bullets.detail: GetEncodedText no longer allocates an intermediate string on the null-terminated fast path, and SKRuntimeEffectUniforms pre-sizes its lookup map to the known uniform count.
The per-type reflection check that determines whether to skip registration in the handle dictionary is now cached, removing repeated reflection overhead on hot object-construction paths.
SKData.SaveTo no longer copies the buffer twice; it now streams directly, halving memory use for large data saves.

bullets.lead: FreeType font rendering on Windows Nano Server
bullets.detail: Nano Server environments lack the GDI font stack. SkiaSharp now uses FreeType on Nano Server, enabling text rendering in containerised Windows workloads that was previously broken.

bullets.lead: Azure Linux, Alpine/musl, and Nano Server test targets
bullets.detail: Containerised CI test legs for Azure Linux, Alpine (musl libc), and Nano Server continuously validate SkiaSharp across these production-relevant environments.

bullets.lead: Windows MSVC environment initialized once per native build
bullets.detail: The MSVC environment setup is now shared across build steps instead of re-run for each target, reducing Windows native build times.

contributor_summaries.jeffska: Implemented FreeType font support for Windows Nano Server, unblocking text rendering in GDI-less container environments.
contributor_summaries.mmitche: Optimized Windows native builds by initializing the MSVC environment once per build instead of per target.
contributor_summaries.ramezgerges: Authored the Graphite GPU backend bindings for Vulkan, Metal, and Dawn.

harfbuzz_summary: HarfBuzzSharp 14.2.1 ships unchanged from 4.151.0, with no new API changes in this release.
